title: Rosemary and Garlic Roast Potatoes
changes_from_base: Oil infused with rosemary and garlic; the fried garlic and rosemary plus parsley tossed through at the end.
summary: This follows the classic roast potato method, but the oil is first infused with rosemary and garlic, and the fried garlic, rosemary and fresh parsley are tossed back through the potatoes at the end.

ingredients.item: floury potatoes (such as Maris Piper, King Edward or russet), peeled
fine salt, for the parboiling water
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Heat the Oven
steps.text: Preheat the oven to 230°C (210°C fan) at least 20 minutes ahead, so the tin is ready to go the moment the potatoes are roughed up.

steps.title: Make the Rosemary Garlic Oil
steps.text: Heat the oil with the rosemary and garlic in the small saucepan over medium heat, stirring, until the garlic is just pale gold, about 3 minutes. Strain immediately into the large bowl, keeping the crisp garlic and rosemary aside, since garlic left in for the whole roast would simply burn, which is why it's fried briefly first and added back only at the end.

steps.title: Cut and Parboil the Potatoes
steps.text: Cut the peeled potatoes into 5 cm chunks, then bring the water to the boil with the salt and bicarbonate of soda, add the potatoes and simmer for about 10 minutes, until a knife meets little resistance at the edges.

steps.title: Rough Up the Surface
steps.text: Drain and leave to rest for a minute, then shake hard in the colander until the surfaces turn to a rough, starchy paste. This texture is what lets the crust form once the potatoes hit the oil.

steps.title: Toss in the Oil and Roast
steps.text: Toss the potatoes through the rosemary garlic oil to coat, spread them out in the tin and roast for 20 minutes. Turn, then roast for a further 20-30 minutes, until deep golden and crisp.

steps.title: Toss With the Fried Garlic and Herbs
steps.text: Toss the hot potatoes with the reserved fried garlic and rosemary, the chopped parsley, salt and pepper, then serve straight away while everything is still warm and fragrant.

tips: Common mistake: leaving raw garlic and rosemary in the tin for the full roast — they burn and turn bitter, so fry them briefly in the oil first and add them back only at the end.
Watch the garlic closely while frying; pale gold is the point to stop, as it darkens quickly after that.
Strain the oil straight away once the garlic is ready, rather than leaving it in the hot pan to carry on cooking.
Toss the fresh parsley through right at the end, off the heat, so it stays bright rather than wilting.
Give the potatoes the same rough shake as the classic method before roasting — the rosemary oil won't make up for a smooth, unroughened surface.
storage: Keep in the fridge for up to 3 days; reheat on a tray in a hot oven at around 200°C (180°C fan) until piping hot (74°C) and crisp again. They freeze well for up to 2 months, though it's best to add fresh parsley after reheating rather than before freezing. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
